definitions.explanation: A broad plan or vision for something to be created or achieved. Used for large-scale ideas such as urban development plans, novel plots, business strategies, or architectural designs. Implies creative or strategic thinking at a high level.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{構想|こうそう}を{練|ね}る。
examples.english: To work out a new concept.

examples.japanese: {小説|しょうせつ}の{構想|こうそう}はできているが、まだ{書|か}き{始|はじ}めていない。
examples.english: I have the concept for the novel, but I haven't started writing yet.

examples.japanese: {市長|しちょう}は{駅前|えきまえ}の{再開発|さいかいはつ}について{壮大|そうだい}な{構想|こうそう}を{発表|はっぴょう}した。
examples.english: The mayor announced a grand vision for the redevelopment of the area in front of the station.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
{構|こう} (to construct, to plan) + {想|そう} (thought, idea). Literally "constructed thought" — a carefully built-up idea.

USAGE:
{構想|こうそう} implies a big-picture plan that has been thought through, but not necessarily finalized or implemented. It is commonly used with {練|ね}る (to work out, to refine) and {立|た}てる (to set up). As a する verb, {構想|こうそう}する means "to conceive a plan."

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {構想|こうそう}を{練|ね}る: to work out / refine a concept
- {構想|こうそう}を{立|た}てる: to formulate a plan
- {構想|こうそう}を{発表|はっぴょう}する: to announce a plan
- {壮大|そうだい}な{構想|こうそう}: a grand vision
- {構想|こうそう}{段階|だんかい}: planning stage
